contexts.text: An aromatic odour, like that of an embalmed corpse: when the celestial Angels are present, what is cadaverous is perceived as aromatic. AC 1518. HH 449.
They who bear internecine hatred... are kept in the deepest cadaverous Hell, where there is a strong stench as from corpses. They prefer this stench to the most delightful odours. SE 1279. SE 1288.
Such are like birds which fly round a carcase; for such faith is the bird, and the carcase is the man without charity.
They are of a livid colour, such as is that of corpses.
There exhaled from them the sphere of a cadaverous stench. SE 3356.
With man, everything is dead, nay cadaverous.
With those whose worship is called Babel, there is no internal worship, but there is something dead, in fact cadaverous, within, which is worshipped.
He smelt his own cadaverous stench.
When the sphere of those who have lived in grievous hatred and revenge, and in cruelty, is turned into odours, there is a cadaverous stench. AC 1860.
Where the carcase is, there are the eagles.
As they exhale a filthy idea of self, their delight is there turned into a cadaverous stench, whereby they are made sensible of the Hell of self. AC 2363. AC 8945:4. SE 3660. SE 3665.

Wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together () = that confirmations of falsities through reasonings will be multiplied in the vastated Church. When the Church is devoid of the good and thence of the truth of faith... it is said to be dead... and therefore is compared to a carcase. AC 3901:end.

The actual evil which a man receives by his own fault is signified in the Word by a carcase; hence in the Ancient and Jewish Churches, it was forbidden to eat what died of its own accord, or a carcase. Illustrated.
They appeared with a ghastly face, as it were cadaverous, so that they might be called effigies of death. AC 4533. AC 4798. SE 2580. SE 3455:end.
Falls back to the corpse...
Some saw their own corpse through my eyes...

Two or three times there breathed on me a cadaverous odour... It was from the Hell where were foul robbers, and assassins, and those who committed crimes with grievous deceit... When there was an excrementitious mingled with a cadaverous odour it came from the Hell where are adulterers who are also cruel. AC 7161:4.
From the caverns, there exhaled a cadaverous stench; the reason was that the cruel and deceitful were therein, to whom a cadaverous odour is most delightful.
That which has perished by evils is called a carcase.
A heap of carcases, and no end of bodies () = that there are innumerable evils, and those who are in evils.
Profaned truth there stinks like a corpse.
Truth without good... is like a body without a soul... and if in place of good there is evil, it is like a corpse.
He hath filled with dead bodies () = thus spiritual death, which is a total deprivation of truth and good.
To eat a carcase, and what has been torn () = the appropriation of evil and falsity.
They who have hankered for revenge, and have thence contracted a fierce and cruel nature, love cadaverous things; and are in such Hells.
They who were in the neglect and contempt of truth appeared livid, like corpses.
This heresy stinks there like a carcase. AR 875:3.
If the understanding alone were healed, man would become like a corpse embalmed, or covered with spices and roses, which would soon derive a stench from the corpse.
In the light of Heaven, satans appear like corpses.
Man then becomes a spiritual corpse.
When a man has led an evil life, he there emits a stench like that from a corpse...
Works without faith are like a body without a soul, thus like a corpse...
When they acted against love with interior deceit... the Spirits fled, and cried out that they could not endure so cadaverous an odour...
On cadaverous Spirits.
Like ravens to a carcase.
Where the carcase is, there are the ravens.
Sirens at last become like corpses... and have a cadaverous smell, which they carry about with them; the reason is, that they desire nothing else than to return into worldly and corporeal things.

They sit on coffins, in which there are corpses; some sit on the corpses themselves; some on the bones; in that light they also appear like ghastly corpses; because they adore what is dead, and deny what is alive.

They are at last sent into Hell, where they lie like corpses, some in bed, some on the earth; and there they are as it were half-dead, with ghastly faces, for 10, 50, 100, 1000, 2000 years... SE 5634.
On a cadaverous bosom from the violation of marriage... Such violaters are in the cadaverous Hell.
Those are called slain who have perished by falsities; and those corpses, who have perished by evils. AE 405:46.

A dead body () = the man of the Church without spiritual life, which he has through truths from the Word, on the extinction of which life he lusts for nothing but falsities, and is averse to truths; thus he becomes dead, and, in the spiritual sense, a corpse.
In its carcase he found a swarm of bees and honey () = that after that faith has been dissipated, in its place there succeeds the good of charity.
Nothing is more delightful than a cadaverous stench to those who have been assassins and poisoners, also to those who have perceived delight in violating women.
A carcase trodden under foot () = an infernal Spirit with whom everything is spiritually dead, in consequence of good being utterly destroyed.
